design_corrections: Intent admission bounds are the accepted legacy proxy (estimated_tokens 1024-8192, request_bytes 1-7168), not the wider bounds written in design section 12.1.
No partial unique index on interaction_id: the original table already declares interaction_id UNIQUE.
Two deferred constraint triggers are added so the database itself refuses an admission or send authorization against changed authority; the design listed only shape and guard changes.
The intent branch is a complete third branch with its own null rules, because the frozen gateway branch requires verifier and proposed-generation fields to be non-null.
Revision 2: migration file names contain _ai_verification_ so the frozen upgrade test excludes them from its historical boundary.
Revision 2: the attempt trigger carries a WHEN clause, so an out-of-order 3c-1 reversal refuses instead of orphaning the trigger.
Revision 3 (text only): the late FOR SHARE reads can complete a lock cycle for a writer that skipped the canonical locks; the writer-lock invariant is a stated condition.
limitations: The listings were rehearsed only in a disposable PostgreSQL database by the package author; that is not the authorized execution and not an independent review.
The frozen PostgreSQL suites were not run with the new migrations present, because that requires creating migration files.
The refusal branch 'AI invocation receipt binding' was not exercised; query plans were not assessed at realistic volume.
Lifecycle writes in the race rehearsals were SQL reproductions of what the PHP services write.
Baseline evidence remains the partitioned 3c-1 checkpoint; it is not one uninterrupted clean execution.
